description:
Finding (investigated at c768670cd, stack #274 top with fz-sc8.124/.125/.126; evidence in the OptionParser session scratchpad s127/): the callback rule is real but small, and the obvious fix costs more than it saves.

The rule: visit_protocol_callback (src/compiler2/jobs/keying.rs ~648) sets local_result = Whole for every non-receiver argument, because a callback has no body and cannot know what its implementations return. Shrunk program (s127/member.fz): three Enum.member?([:a, :b], needle) calls key Enum.member?/2 three times, one per needle, where one serves. In one OptionParser.parse call this is 7 excess keys of 72 (Enum.member?/2 has 9 keys: 7 from needle literals, 2 from the receiver type, which is real dispatch). It is the same 7 keys in fixtures 00761/00762/00765 (7 of 186 excess in 00761).

Why the rule exists: without it two callers differing only in an accumulator literal share a key and blend. Shown on a user protocol (s127/proto.fz): making every callback argument Ignore blends Via.keeps's two callers into {:first | :second, int}.

Spiked fix A (s127/spike127.diff): a callback's returned demand is the join of every implementation's own returned demand, waiting on each implementation's InputDemand. Keys fall by 7 per program (distinct1 214 -> 207) and Enum.member?/2 goes 3 -> 1 on the shrunk program, output identical. But jobs RISE by about 250 per program (distinct1 2584 -> 2844) because every Enumerable implementation module is pulled in to be asked, debug CPU is flat or worse (1.68 -> 1.75s), and it reverses fz-afu.11's contract (a protocol callback reads no implementation demand; 7 compiler2 pins fail, 5 toward more work). Variant B (join only implementations already dispatched, no waits) saves the 7 keys and a few jobs but is order-dependent, the design fz-afu.11 removed. Receiver type is not known when InputDemand is derived, so a per-receiver join cannot be expressed there.

Not tried: answering the returned axis from the callback's declared return type (a callback declared to return boolean cannot return its needle). That would read no implementation. Needs the protocol's callback specs to be available to DeriveInputDemand; unverified.

Related, measured, not this ticket: a guard comparing to a literal (mode == :strict) and a pinned pattern key per literal; Keyword.get/3-style functions key per returned literal for result-type precision only.

Do not build without a page that shows a variant saving both keys and jobs.
title: A protocol callback's non-receiver arguments are keyed only where an implementation returns them
